environment.tool: manual audit of the final tag source + live compiled binary; raw-socket client sending exact bytes, strict-token upstream peer logging verbatim request bytes and byte count

findings.description: `GET /api%2fexec%3fcmd=id` reproduces byte-for-byte, 3/3 cold, exactly one `?`, exec runs. `:63` guards only `#`, `\\` and a UTF-8 check with no `c<32` test, so `%09` and `%0a` are accepted here and 400 on the sibling builds: the upstream line carries a literal TAB or LF inside token 2. `:63` also splits with `getline(ss, part, '/')`, so a decoded LF terminates a stream segment as well as reaching the line. Sink is `:67` `l.uri + path.substr(l.path.size()) + query`.
findings.title: Same decode-only query injection, and this guard has no control-character test, so decoded TAB and LF pass into the upstream request line

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
